---
title: "Comping rhythm: Red Garland"
subtitle: "For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Red Garland**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

Chords on the and of 2 and the and of 4. The second one anticipates the next bar's chord and is held across the barline.

It belongs in *Swing*. Here it is in the swing style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Red Garland","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Charleston

Start with something simpler. A held chord on beat 1 and a short one on the and of 2. The first comping rhythm most players learn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-charleston.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Charleston","opts":{"compRhythm":"charleston"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Off-beats

Chords on the and of 1 and the and of 3, never on a downbeat.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-offbeats.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Off-beats","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Red Garland, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Chords on the and of 2 and the and of 4; the second one is the next bar's chord, early, held across the barline. The anticipation pulls the band forward.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="84" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Red Garland","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}},{"label":"Off-beats (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"offbeats"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 120 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Red Garland","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|A7|Dm7|G7|Cmaj7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Red Garland","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}}]'></div>

## Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="swing" data-chart="Dm7 G7|Em7 A7|Dm7 G7|Cmaj7" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Red Garland","opts":{"compRhythm":"garland"}}]'></div>
